t.5.64.1: Thus addressed by Hanumān, Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, pressed that jewel to his heart and wept, together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.5.64.2: But on seeing that finest of jewels, Rāghava, worn down by grief, spoke these words to Sugrīva with eyes brimming with tears.
t.5.64.3: Just as a cow, tender toward her calf, flows with milk out of love for it, so too does my heart melt at the sight of this jewel, the finest of gems.
t.5.64.4: This precious jewel was given to Vaidehī by my father-in-law at the time of her wedding; fastened upon her head, it shines with surpassing splendor.
t.5.64.5: For this jewel, born of the waters and honored by the foremost, was given at a sacrifice by the wise Śakra, who was supremely pleased.
t.5.64.6: Seeing this finest of jewels, O gentle one, today I feel I have come to the sight of my father, and likewise of the lord Vaideha.
t.5.64.8: What did Sītā, the princess of Videha, say? Tell me again and again, gentle one, for she sprinkles me with the water of her words as one sprinkles water upon a man who is lifeless.
t.5.64.7: For this jewel shines upon the head of that beloved of mine; today, by the sight of it, I think of her as though she had been regained.
t.5.64.9: What could be more grievous than this, O Saumitri, that I behold this water-born jewel come to me without Vaidehī?
t.5.64.11: Lead me too to that place where my beloved was seen. Having received news of her, I could not remain here even for a moment.
t.5.64.10: If Vaidehī will hold on for a month, she lives long indeed; but I, gentle one, could not live even a moment without her, the dark-eyed one.
t.5.64.12: How does she, my lovely-hipped one, most timid of the timid, now stand in the midst of those dreadful rākṣasas who inspire terror?
t.5.64.14: What did Sītā say, O Hanumān? Tell me truly. By this alone shall I live, as a sick man lives by medicine.
t.5.64.13: Surely her face, surrounded by the rākṣasas, does not shine, just as the autumn moon, rising out of the darkness, does not shine when it is veiled by clouds.
t.5.64.15: Hanuman, tell me: what did my sweet, sweet-spoken lady say, that fair-hipped one, bereft of me? Having passed from sorrow into still greater sorrow, how does Jānakī live?
